notes: do_spike has no GET_SKILL/class check; the POS_STANDING command-table gate is the only entry gate (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
The registered POS_STANDING gate is pinned by the native command registration test; shared dispatcher bytes belong to the command-gate matrix (R2/R5b/R5c).

Normal command dispatch rejects a fighting-position caller before do_spike; the handler's internal FIGHTING branch is reachable only through a direct non-dispatch caller such as breed_killer (R2/R5b/R5c/R5e).
An awake, non-fighting caller receives the exact target prompt (R1/R3/R5e).
A missing visible-room target reaches C's direct NOPERSON branch (R1/R2/R3/R5e).
An innate-werewolf NPC target with no wielded spike reaches the exact wielded-item refusal (R1/R3/R5e).
The peaceful-room murder refusal is the shared combat-protection boundary; do_spike contributes no unique state beyond its exact literal (R1/R5b/R5c/R5e).
The suicide refusal is pinned in the existing focused handler test (R1/R4/R5e).
Werewolf mode is tested as an AFF_WEREWOLF requirement before own-kind and immortality checks (R1/R4/R5e).
The attacker's PLR_WEREWOLF refusal is pinned for spike (R1/R4/R5e).
A mortal attacker cannot destroy an immortal target after the earlier gates (R1/R4/R5e).
C's get_char_room_vis accepts an affected NPC; the handler preserves the same target-affect, own-kind, and immortal checks without inventing a player-only branch (R1/R4/R5e).
The successful mob target exposes actor and room audiences, with no NPC victim descriptor bytes (R1/R3/R5e).
A successful NPC spike reaches the raw_kill extraction path and removes the mob without combat XP/kills invention (R1/R3/R4/R5e).
The level-gap failure emits all three miss audiences and waits two violence pulses; the random comparison is covered by the focused test (R1/R3/R5e).
A successful player target clears both PLR nightbreed flags, updates PK/death counters, and reaches raw_kill with no invented combat damage (R1/R3/R4/R5e).
The level comparison and inclusive number(0,LEVEL_IMMORT) success arm are isolated from the shared RNG/combat matrix (R3/R5e).

breed_killer directly invokes do_spike/do_stake for autonomous mob attacks; its caller is owned by the special-procedure cityguard/breed inventory and is not duplicated under the player command surface (R2/R5b/R5c/R5e).
Stake uses the same C handler with SCMD_STAKE; spike owns the shared handler matrix while stake remains a later source-order command row (R2/R5b/R5c/R5e).
